summary.text: Christian Furman is the Democratic candidate for Kentucky State Senate District 6 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against Republican incumbent Lindsey Tichenor.
A geriatrics and palliative care physician and member of the Prospect City Council, she won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Chaz Stoess.

paragraphs.text: Furman has a bachelor's degree from the University of Miami (1992) and an M.D. from the University of Louisville (1996), according to Ballotpedia.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she was born in Louisville, raised in Crestwood and graduated from Oldham County High School.

She said she completed her residency and fellowship at the University of Louisville, worked as a geriatrics and palliative care physician with leadership roles at the university and the VA hospital, and completed a Congressional Fellowship in Washington, D.C., advising on older adults' issues.
She said she and her husband raised two children in Oldham County and that she serves on the Prospect City Council.
Furman described her campaign around an affordable, healthier and safer Kentucky, and said she is also passionate about public schools and universal Pre-K.
She listed endorsements from AFT Kentucky 1360, former U.S. Representative Mike Ward, Prospect Mayor Doug Farnsley and former Pewee Valley Mayor Clayton Stoess.
